title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: booking the amendment fee on a signed amendment
content:
## When this applies
Under the Dangerous Goods Acceptance product, the amendment fee falls due from the state of an acceptance's records once the shipper has signed an amendment declaration. The fee is settled once for each chargeable signed amendment declaration, on the acceptance that declaration amends: a chargeable amendment is booked as one amendment-fee row that references that amendment submission, and an amendment that is free books no row at all. This policy sets only the amount of the fee. The amendment's own conditions — the amendment deadline before the cargo cut-off, the maximum number of signed amendments, the permitted weight change and container increase, and the sailing allotment — continue to govern both the signed amendment and its fee, and this policy adds no condition to them.

## Business effect
Booking the fee writes one amendment-fee charge, dated on the day of booking, on the acceptance's dangerous-goods account, and raises the charges the acceptance owes by the amount booked. The action itself attaches the charge to the most recently signed amendment declaration of the acceptance that no amendment-fee charge references yet — between two signed at the same moment, the one with the higher declaration reference — and records that declaration's reference on the charge and in the receipt. Declarations awaiting signature, returned for correction or withdrawn are never attached. A call whose charge already exists — same acceptance, same booking, same attached declaration and same amount — writes nothing further and leaves the balance unchanged.

## How it is invoked
The action is book_dg_amendment_fee_40feddd0, an internal tool that must first be unlocked (unlock_agent_discoverable_tool) and then called (call_agent_discoverable_tool) by the agent.

## Parameters
| Parameter | What it is | Format |
|---|---|---|
| dg_id | reference number of the dangerous-goods acceptance whose declaration was amended, as shown by the dangerous-goods acceptance lookup | identifier, text |
| booking_id | reference number of the booking the goods travel under, as shown on the acceptance record | identifier, text |
| amount_usd | the amendment fee to book | US dollars, 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before the call |

No declaration reference is passed: the action resolves by itself which signed amendment declaration the charge attaches to.

## Return
The receipt lists dg_event_id (reference of the new charge), dg_id, submission_id (reference of the signed amendment declaration the charge is attached to; empty when every signed amendment already has a charge), charge_code (always amendment_fee), amount_usd (the fee booked, 2 decimal places) and charges_due_usd (the acceptance's outstanding dangerous-goods charges after the fee, 2 decimal places). The call has succeeded when the receipt returns the new charge reference, the declaration it is attached to and the booked amount. No other outcome is defined for this action.

## Contract Q&A
- *Does the action work out the fee?* No. It records the amount passed in; the amount and whether a fee is owed are decided from the published rules and the records before the call.
- *Does the agent tell the action which amendment to charge?* No. The action looks up the acceptance's declaration file and attaches the charge itself; that look-up involves no amount, eligibility or prerequisite.
- *Is an amendment that is free booked with an amount of 0.00?* No row is booked for a free amendment.
